title: A Fairer Way to Split the Bill
scene: Four friends share two pizzas at lunch but order different drinks. When the bill arrives, Maya gently questions an even split, suggests a fairer method, and they agree without making anyone uncomfortable.
sceneJa: 友人4人でピザを2枚分け合った昼食。飲み物は各自で違うものを注文した。会計を均等に割ろうとしたところ、マヤが控えめに確認し、食事と飲み物を分けて計算する方法を提案。気まずくならずに納得できる支払い方を決める。

chunks.en: four of us had shared two pizzas,
chunks.ja: 4人でピザを2枚分け合ったけれど
飲み物はそれぞれ違うものを頼んでいた

chunks.en: As I started splitting the bill evenly,
chunks.ja: 僕が会計を均等に割ろうとすると

chunks.en: Maya said, 'I might be missing something,
chunks.ja: マヤが「私が何か見落としているかもしれないけど

chunks.en: but doesn't this include the drinks?'
chunks.ja: これって飲み物代も入ってるよね？」と言った

chunks.en: 'Would it make more sense to split the food four ways
chunks.ja: 「食事代は4人で均等に分けて

chunks.en: and pay for our own drinks?'
chunks.ja: 飲み物は各自で払うほうがよくない？」と
「確かにそうだね」と僕は言い
「そこまで考えてなかったよ」と続けた
「一緒に計算しよう」と僕が言い

chunks.en: and Maya read out the drink prices
chunks.ja: マヤが飲み物の金額を読み上げ
みんなが「それでいいよ」と納得して

chunks.en: and we went back to arguing
chunks.ja: 僕らはまた議論に戻った

chunks.en: about which pizza had been better.
chunks.ja: どっちのピザがおいしかったかという話に

questions.question: Which split keeps Maya's cautious clarification as a natural speaking unit?
options: I might be missing something, / but doesn't this include the drinks?
I might / be missing something but doesn't / this include the drinks?
I might be missing / something but / doesn't this include the drinks?
questions.explanation: 'I might be missing something' is a complete softening phrase. It signals uncertainty before raising a question.

questions.question: What does 'Would it make more sense to ...?' suggest here?
options: The speaker insists that the only possible choice is hers.
The speaker gently proposes a more reasonable way to split the cost.
The speaker asks whether the receipt is fake.
questions.explanation: This tentative question invites discussion. The proposal separates shared food from individually ordered drinks.

questions.question: Why does Maya bring up the drinks before the bill is split?
options: She wants someone else to pay for everything.
She is trying to avoid paying for the pizza.
Different drink orders could make an equal split unfair, so she suggests checking the calculation.
questions.explanation: Maya is not accusing anyone; she flags an overlooked detail and proposes a fair solution.

speak: Imagine: you and friends shared food but ordered different drinks. Read: notice Maya's gentle tone. Chunk: practise 'I might be missing something', 'Would it make more sense to ...?', and 'Let's work it out' as full units. Understand: the first softens a question, the second proposes an option, and the third invites joint action. Check: answer the three questions. Speak (30 seconds): raise a possible issue with a shared bill, propose a fairer split, and agree on a calculation. Final Read: read all six sentences without Japanese; pause after 'I might be missing something' and keep the proposal friendly.
review: New: 'I might be missing something' (見落としているかもしれない), 'Would it make more sense to ...?' (〜するほうが筋が通るかな), 'Let's work it out' (一緒に解決・計算しよう). Reuse Lesson 101/104 'Fair enough' for a cost-sharing concern rather than a plan or boundary; Lesson 101 'That works for me' for a payment method rather than a return arrangement. Compared with Lessons 93–106, this focuses on fair cost-sharing and collaborative arithmetic, not a plan change or declining an invitation. Sources: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/make-sense ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/work-out .
